name: Currant Wine No. 1
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: less than a pound of sugar to a quart of the mashed fruit
ingredients.originalText: less than a pound of sugar to a quart of the mashed fruit

ingredients.name: a small quantity of brandy or whisky
ingredients.originalText: a small quantity of brandy or whisky
ingredients.quantityText: a small quantity of brandy or whisky

instructions.text: Stem, mash and strain the currants
Add a half pint of water and less than a pound of sugar to a quart of the mashed fruit
Stir well up together and pour into a clean cask, leaving the bung-hole open, or covered with a piece of lace
Let it stand for a month to ferment
Just before bottling you may add a small quantity of brandy or whisky

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Stem, mash and strain the currants
2. Add a half pint of water and less than a pound of sugar to a quart of the mashed fruit
3. Stir well up together and pour into a clean cask, leaving the bung-hole open, or covered with a piece of lace
4. Let it stand for a month to ferment
5. Just before bottling you may add a small quantity of brandy or whisky
